Naturally forming the seven jewels, gathered horizontally into the myriad things, light, brilliance, and purity all emerging, good and excellent beyond compare. Dwelling above and below nothing, reaching through to boundless limits.

Each of you should diligently advance, and strive to seek it yourself. You will surely transcend and depart, and be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss. Cutting across the five destinies, the evil paths close by themselves. The supreme Way without limit is easy to reach, yet no one goes; that land does not oppose or reject, and is naturally drawn along. Cast away the will, as empty as space, diligently practice to seek the Way and virtue. You can attain the most ultimate long life, with life and joy without limit. Why cling to worldly affairs, and
nao
worry about impermanence?

The people of the world all contend over affairs of no urgency; amid this extremely evil and utterly bitter world, they toil at business to provide for themselves. High and low, rich and poor, young and old, men and women, with accumulated thoughts and piled-up cares, they run about for the mind. Without fields they worry about fields, without houses they worry about houses; for family and wealth, whether having or lacking, they worry alike.

Having one, they want another; thinking to be equal with all. Just when they have a little, they worry again about unforeseen events. Water, fire, robbers, enemies, creditors—burning, washing away, plundering, extorting—scattered and destroyed. The mind is miserly and the will fixed, unable to let go. At the end of life, they abandon and discard it, and none follows them. Rich and poor alike, all this bitter sorrow in a thousand different ways.

The people of the world—fathers and sons, brothers, husbands and wives, relatives—should love and respect one another, without hatred or jealousy. Whether having or lacking, they should share; they should not be greedy or miserly. Speech and countenance should always be harmonious, without opposing one another. Sometimes the mind contends, and there is anger or resentment; in later lives it grows more and more intense, until it becomes a great enmity. The affairs of the world do harm to one another; even if it does not happen at once, one should think of it as already broken.

People, amid love and desire, are born alone and die alone, come alone and go alone; the suffering and joy are their own, and none can take their place. Good and evil transform, and follow them to the place of birth; the paths differ, and the chance to meet is without a set time. Why not, while strong and healthy, diligently practice goodness? What do you wait for?

The good and evil of the world, one cannot see for oneself; auspiciousness and misfortune, fortune and calamity, are each contended for and made. The body is foolish and the spirit dark, and turning to receive other teachings, inverted and continuous, is the root of impermanence. Blindly and stubbornly, they do not believe the sutra-Dharma. The mind with no far-reaching concern, each wanting quick gratification. Deluded in anger and hatred, greedy for wealth and sex. Never stopping; alas, pitiable!

Their forebears were not good, did not recognize virtue and the Way, and no one spoke of it—there is surely no wonder in this. The course of death and birth, the paths of good and evil, they all do not believe, saying there is none such. They look upon one another, and only see this.

Some fathers weep for sons, some sons weep for fathers; brothers, husbands and wives, weep for one another. One dies and one lives, and they cling to each other. Bound by love and sorrow, there is never a time of release. Thinking of kindness and affection, they never leave the bonds of emotion and desire. Unable to think deeply and plan carefully, single-mindedly practicing the Way. Their years and lives soon end, and there is nothing to be done!

Those deluded about the Way are many; those who awaken to the Way are few. Each harbors the poison of killing, evil atmosphere dark and dim. Doing evil, they rise up to cause affairs, opposing heaven and earth. Giving free rein to their crimes to the utmost, suddenly their lives are snatched away. Falling below into the evil paths, with no time of emerging.

You should reflect and plan carefully, distance yourselves from all evil, choose the good, and diligently practice it. Love and desire, glory and splendor, cannot be forever preserved; all must be parted from, and there is nothing to delight in. Diligently advancing, you should be reborn in the Land of Bliss. Wisdom bright and penetrating, merit supreme. Do not follow the mind's desires, and fail in the sutra-precepts, lagging behind others.

blocks.text: Chapter 34: The Mind Cleared and Illumined

inline.s: Maitreya said: The Buddha's words and teachings, deeply profound and very good. All receive his kind grace, and are freed from sorrow and suffering. The Buddha is the king of Dharma, exalted beyond all sages, his light shining through and reaching everywhere without limit, universally the teacher of devas and humans. Now that we have met the Buddha, and again heard the name of Measureless Life, none is without joy, and the mind is cleared and illumined.

The Buddha told Maitreya: To revere the Buddha is great goodness. Truly one should be mindful of the Buddha, cut off all fox-like doubt, pull out all love and desire, and close off all sources of evil. Wandering in the three worlds without obstruction, revealing the right path and saving those not yet saved.

You should know that the people of the ten directions, from endless aeons past, turning in the six paths, have sorrow and suffering without cease. In birth there is painful suffering; in old age also painful suffering; in illness, utmost painful suffering; in death, utmost painful suffering. Foul-smelling and impure, there is nothing to delight in. You should decide for yourselves, wash away the defilement of the mind, be faithful and honest in word and deed, and corresponding within and without.

People can save themselves, and in turn rescue and aid one another. With utmost sincerity seeking the vow, they accumulate the roots of goodness. Though in one life they cultivate diligently and with bitter toil, it is only for a moment; afterward they are born in the Land of Measureless Life, with peace and joy without limit. Forever cutting off the root of birth and death, without again the calamity of suffering; with life of a thousand million aeons, free and at ease.
Each of you should diligently advance, seeking what your mind desires. Do not doubt or regret, and bring faults upon yourselves
(jiu)
, being born in the borderland, the city of seven jewels, and receiving all kinds of distress for five hundred years.
Maitreya said: Receiving the Buddha's clear instruction, I will single-mindedly study and practice, respectfully following and practicing it, not daring to have any doubt.

blocks.text: Chapter 35: The Sufferings of a Defiled World

inline.s: The Buddha told Maitreya: You are able, in this world, to rectify your minds and upright your intentions, not doing all evil, which is great virtue. Why? In the worlds of the ten directions, good is more and evil less, and beings are easily taught and transformed. This five-evil world alone, suffering is most severe. I have now become Buddha here, teaching and transforming all beings, causing them to renounce the five evils, remove the five pains, and leave the five burnings, subduing and transforming their minds, causing them to hold the five goods and obtain their merit and virtue.

What are the five? The first is: the classes of beings in the world desire to do much evil. The strong oppress the weak, in turn attacking and destroying one another, harming, killing, and wounding, devouring
(dan)
one another. Not knowing to do good, afterward they receive calamity and punishment; therefore there are the poor and beggars, the orphaned and solitary, the deaf and blind, the dumb
(yin)
and mute, the foolish and wicked, the crippled
wang

and mad. All because in former lives they did not believe virtue and the Way, and were unwilling to do good. Those who are noble, wealthy, and eminent, worthy and wise elders, brave, wise, and gifted men, are all from the compassionate filial piety of past lives, cultivating good and accumulating merit.

In the world there are these things, plainly evident before the eyes. After the end of life, they enter the dark realm, being reborn and receiving a body, changing form and changing the path. Therefore there are the hells, the beasts, the flying and creeping creatures. For example, like the prisons of the world, with extreme suffering and the utmost punishments; the soul and vital spirit, following sins, head toward
(this is a loan for 'head')

their destination. The life they receive, sometimes long, sometimes short, arises together with their companions, and they repay one another. Until the calamitous evil is exhausted, they can never depart. Turning within it, for many aeons, hard to emerge. Hard to attain liberation; the pain is beyond words. Between heaven and earth, there naturally is this. Even if it does not immediately respond, good and evil will surely return to them.

The second is: the people of the world do not follow the law and standards, but are extravagant, licentious, proud, and wanton, following their own minds as they please. Those above are not clear-minded, and those in office are not upright, entrapping the wronged and injuring the loyal and good. The mind and the mouth differ, deceitful and false in many ways. High and low, within and without, in turn deceive and cheat one another. Angry, malicious, and foolish, wishing to enrich only themselves, wishing to be greedy to possess more. In profit and loss, victory and defeat, they accumulate anger and create enmity, destroying their homes and losing their lives, not concerned with what came before or after. The rich are miserly and stingy, unwilling to give. Loving, guarding, and greedy, the heart is toiled and the body suffers. Thus to the end, none follows them. Good and evil, fortune and calamity, pursue the life they are born into, sometimes in a place of joy, sometimes entering bitter suffering.
Or again, seeing the good, they hate and slander, not thinking to admire and follow. Always harboring a thieving mind, coveting
xi

others' profit to supply themselves, and when it is spent, they acquire it again. The spirit knows and records, and in the end they enter the evil paths. Naturally having the three destinies, with measureless suffering, turning within them, for many aeons hard to emerge; the pain is beyond words.

The third is: the people of the world, depending on one another in their lives, how long is their lifespan? People of no goodness have body and mind not upright. Always harboring evil thoughts, always thinking of lust
yi
. The breast filled with vexation, the depraved state leaking outward. Wasting the family wealth, doing what is unlawful. What should be sought, they are unwilling to do.

Or again, they form alliances and assemblies, and raise armies to attack one another. Attacking, plundering, and killing, forcibly seizing and threatening, providing for wives and children, and making boundless pleasure. The multitudes all loathe and resent them, suffering and finding them bitter. Such evils, cling to both humans and ghosts. The spirit records and remembers, and they themselves enter the three destinies. With measureless suffering, turning within them; for many aeons hard to emerge; the pain is beyond words.

The fourth is: the people of the world do not think of cultivating goodness. Double-tongued, evil-mouthed, false words, and flattering speech. Hating and envying good people, ruining the worthy and wise. Not filial to parents, slighting teachers and elders. Friends without trust, rarely attaining sincerity. Noble and self-important, saying they have the Way. Tyrannical and powerful, insulting others. Wanting people to fear and respect them, without shame or fear. Always harboring arrogance, hard to tame or transform.

Relying on the merit and virtue of their former lives to protect them, now in this life doing evil, the merit and virtue is exhausted and extinguished. When life finally ends, all the evils return to surround them. Again their name and record are written in the spirit. Calamities and faults pull at them, with no place to release. They can only go forward, entering the fire and crucible
huo
. Body and mind crushed, spirit and form in utmost suffering. At such a time, what use is repentance?

The fifth is: the people of the world are shiftless and lazy, unwilling to do good, nor cultivate the body and pursue their work. Against their parents' teaching, they oppose and rebel. Like a mortal enemy, it would be better to have no child. Ungrateful and contrary to righteousness, with no repayment. Wanton and wandering, addicted to wine and fond of fine food. Rough and violent
hu
and stubborn, not knowing human feeling. Without righteousness or courtesy, impossible to remonstrate. For the six relatives and kindred, and whether resources suffice, they cannot be concerned.

Not thinking of their parents' kindness, not preserving the righteousness of teachers and friends. The mind intends body and mouth, yet there is not even one good deed. Not believing the Buddha's sutras and Dharma, not believing birth and death, good and evil. Wanting to harm the Sage-realities, and to stir up discord among the communities of monks. Ignorant, dark, and deluded, taking themselves to be wise. Not knowing whence birth comes, nor to what death goes. Not benevolent and not compliant, wishing for long life. With kind teaching they are unwilling to believe. Speaking earnestly to them, it does no good. Within the mind, blocked and closed, the intention not opening or understanding. When the great end of life approaches, repentance and fear come together. Not having cultivated goodness beforehand, they repent only at the last. Repenting afterward, what can be done?

Between heaven and earth, the six paths are clearly distinguished. Good and evil receive retribution, fortune and calamity succeed each other; the body itself undergoes it, with none to take its place. Those who do good, walking in goodness, go from joy to joy, from light to light. Those who do evil, walking in evil, go from suffering to suffering, from darkness to darkness. Who can know this? Only the Buddha knows.

Teaching and guiding with words, those who believe and practice are few. Birth and death never rest, and the evil paths never cease. So the people of the world, hard to speak of exhaustively. Therefore there are naturally the three destinies, with measureless suffering, turning within them. Life after life, aeon after aeon, with no time of emerging. Hard to attain liberation; the pain is beyond words.

Thus the five evils, the five pains, and the five burnings, are like a great fire burning the body of a person. If one is able, within this, single-mindedly to control the intention, rectify the body and right mindfulness, with word and deed corresponding, and what is done utmost sincere; alone practicing all goodness, not doing all evil; the body alone freed and liberated, obtaining the merit and virtue, attaining long life and the Way of nirvāṇa. This is the great five goodnesses!

The Buddha told Maitreya: I say to you, thus the five evils, the five pains, and the five burnings arise in succession. Whoever dares to commit these, shall undergo the evil destinies. Or in this present life, first suffer illness and calamity, unable to live or die, showing it to the multitudes to see. Or at the end of life, enter the three evil paths, with sorrow, pain, and cruel poison, burning
jiao
andblazing
(ancient equivalent of 'burning')

With their enemies, in turn killing and wounding one another. From small beginnings, they grow into great hardship. All from greed and clinging to wealth and sex, unwilling to give. Each wanting to please himself, with no regard for right or wrong. Driven by foolish desire, enriching themselves and contending for profit; wealth, honors, glory, and splendor, satisfying the mind for a time. Unable to be patient, not striving to cultivate goodness. The might and power last but a little while, and then waste away. Heaven's Way sets in motion, naturally
grasping
them up, the lone
qiong
and solitary
song
and shaken, entering therein. From ancient times to the present there is this; alas, how pitiful!

You have obtained the Buddha's scriptures and words; reflect carefully upon them, and each of you guard yourself, to the end of life without negligence. Revere the sages, respect goodness, be benevolent, compassionate, and loving. You should seek to pass beyond the world, and pull out and sever the root of all evil of birth and death. You should leave the three destinies, the paths of sorrow, fear, and painful suffering.

As for you doing good, what is the foremost? You should rectify your own minds, and rectify your own bodies; the ears, eyes, mouth, and nose, all should be rectified. Body and mind clean and pure, corresponding with goodness. Do not follow the desires of cravings, and do not violate the evils. Speech and countenance should be harmonious, and the practice of the body should be single-minded. In action and in regard, steadfast and composed, proceeding with ease. Acting in haste, repentance and failure follow after. Doing it without care, one loses the merit.

blocks.text: Chapter 37: Like a Poor Man Who Finds a Treasure

inline.s: You should broadly plant the roots of merit, and do not violate the prohibitions of the Way. Patient, vigorous, single-minded and compassionate, with fasting and precepts pure. For one day and one night, it surpasses doing good for a hundred years in the Land of Measureless Life. Why? In that Buddha-land, all is accumulated merit and good, without even a hair's breadth of evil. In this world cultivating goodness for ten days and ten nights, the merit obtained surpasses doing good for a thousand years in the Buddha-lands of other regions. Why? In the Buddha-lands of other regions, merit and virtue are natural, with no place to commit evil. This world alone has little good and much evil; drinking bitterness and eating poison, never knowing rest.
I

have compassion for you, earnestly teaching and instructing you, and bestow upon you the sutra-Dharma. Hold it all, and reflect upon it; uphold it all and practice it. High and low, men and women, relatives and friends, in turn teach and admonish one another, and mutually restrain themselves. Harmonious and accordant with right principle, joyful, compassionate, and filial. If what is done offends, then repent oneself. Depart from evil and approach good; hearing in the morning and reforming in the evening. Upholding the sutra-precepts, like a poor man who finds a treasure. Reforming the past and cultivating the future, washing
(xi)
the mind and changing conduct. Naturally the response descends, and the wish, as soon as made
zhe
, is attained.

Wherever the Buddha practices, the cities, towns, villages, and settlements, none is not transformed. The world peaceful and harmonious, the sun and moon bright and clear. Wind and rain in their seasons, calamities and plagues do not arise. The country prosperous and the people secure, weapons of war unused. Exalting virtue and promoting benevolence, earnestly practicing courtesy and deference. The land without robbers or thieves, without wrong or injustice. The strong do not oppress the weak, and each obtains what is fitting.

I have compassion for you more than a father and mother think of their children. I have become Buddha in this world, using goodness to attack evil, pulling out the suffering of birth and death. Causing them to attain the five virtues, and ascend to the peace of the unconditioned. When I enter nirvāṇa, the sutras and the Way gradually perish. The people become false and flattering, and again do much evil. The five pains and five burnings, as time passes, grow more severe. You in turn should admonish and instruct one another, according to the Buddha's scriptures and Dharma, and not violate them.

The Bodhisattva Maitreya, with hands pressed together, said: The evil and suffering of the world, is just so, just so. The Buddha, with compassion, has saved and liberated them all. Receiving the Buddha's weighty instruction, I dare not violate or lose it.

blocks.text: Chapter 38: Bowing to the Buddha and Seeing the Land

inline.s: The Buddha told Ānanda: If you wish to see Amitābha Buddha and the land where the bodhisattvas and arhats dwell, you should rise and face the west, at the place where the sun sets, respectfully bow, and with mindfulness recite Namo Amitābha Buddha.

Ānanda then rose from his seat, faced west with hands pressed together, bowed, and said: I now wish to see the Land of Bliss, Amitābha Buddha, to make offerings and serve him, and to plant the roots of goodness.

Between the prostrations, suddenly he beheld the Land of Bliss. Amitābha Buddha, with countenance vast and great, his features dignified and pure, like a mountain of gold, rising high above all the worlds. He also heard the Tathagatas of the worlds in the ten directions, proclaiming and praising the manifold merits of Amitābha Buddha, without obstruction or interruption.

Ānanda said: That Buddha's pure land, I have never attained before; I too wish to be born there. The World-Honored One told him: Those born there have already drawn near to countless Buddhas and planted the roots of all virtues. If you wish to be born there, you should single-mindedly take refuge and gaze upon him.

As he said this, Amitābha Buddha immediately let forth from his palm immeasurable light, universally illumining all the Buddha-worlds. At that time, all the Buddha-lands became clearly manifest, as if within one fathom. Because of the supreme light of Amitābha Buddha, the utmost purity, in this world all the black mountains, the snow mountains, the diamond and iron mountains, the great and small mountains, the rivers and forests, the palaces of devas and humans, all the realms, without exception, are illumined and revealed.

Like the sun rising, bright and illumining the world. Even the hells, the valleys, the dark and obscure places, are all greatly opened up, all becoming one color. Like the water of an aeon filling the world, wherein all things are submerged and invisible, the rolling
huang
and boundless flood, only the great water is seen. The Buddha's light is likewise.

All the lights of the sravakas and bodhisattvas are all hidden, and only the Buddha-light is seen, brightly shining and gloriously manifest. The fourfold assembly of this gathering, the eight classes of devas and dragons, humans and non-humans, all see the Land of Bliss and its manifold adornments.

Amitābha Buddha, upon his high seat, majestic virtue towering, with the marks of excellence and the light of beauty, surrounded by sravakas and bodhisattvas in reverence. Like the king of the Sumeru mountain, emerging from the sea, brightly revealed and shining, pure, clear, and upright. Without any defilement or any class of different forms. Only adorned with the manifold jewels, with sages and worthies dwelling together.

Ānanda and the assemblies of bodhisattvas were all filled with great joy, leaping up and bowing, with heads touching the ground, reciting Namo Amitābha Buddha. The devas and people, even down to the flying and creeping creatures, who beheld this light, all the diseases and suffering, none were not brought to rest; all the sorrow and vexation, none were not liberated. All had compassionate hearts, and doing good, rejoiced and were happy.

Bells and chimes, the lute and the harp, the harp and the many instruments, without being struck, naturally produced the five tones. The devas and people of the Buddha-lands, each holding flowers and incense, came into the sky, scattering them as offerings.

At that time, the Land of Bliss, beyond a hundred thousand million Buddha-lands to the west, by the Buddha's power, was as if before the eyes, like a pure celestial eye viewing a space of one fathom. They who are there see this world likewise. They see the Sahā world, Śākyamuni Tathagata, with the assemblies of monks, surrounding and expounding the Dharma.

At that time the Buddha told Ānanda and the Bodhisattva Maitreya: Do you see the Land of Bliss, its palaces, towers, halls, springs, ponds, forests, and trees, endowed with subtle, wondrous, pure, and adorned qualities or
(ancient equivalent of 'or not')
not? Do you see the devas of the desire realm, up to the Akanistha heaven, raining all fragrant flowers throughout the Buddha-lands or not? Ānanda replied: Yes, I have seen them.
Do you hear Amitābha Buddha proclaiming the great voice, reaching throughout all worlds, transforming beings or not? Ānanda replied: Yes, I have heard.

The Buddha said: Do you see the pure practitioners of that land, roaming in empty space, with palaces following their bodies, without obstruction, reaching to the ten directions to make offerings to the Buddhas, or not? And do you see them, mindful of the Buddha continuously, or not? Again there are many birds, dwelling in the realm of space, producing all kinds of sounds, all of them transformations—do you see them all or not? Maitreya said: As the Buddha has spoken, I see each and every one.

The Buddha told Maitreya: Do you again see those born in the womb of that land? Maitreya said: World-Honored One, I see in the Land of Bliss those dwelling in the womb of the flower, like the heavens of Yama, abiding in palaces. Again I see beings, within the lotus, seated cross-legged
jia fu
, naturally transformed and born, emerging in an instant. For what reason do the people of that land have the womb-born and the transformation-born?

blocks.text: Chapter 40: The Borderland and the City of Doubt

inline.s: The Buddha told Maitreya: If there are beings, with a mind of doubt, cultivating the merits and wishing to be born in that land, not understanding the Buddha's wisdom, the wisdom of the inconceivable, the wisdom of the unmeasurable, the vast wisdom of the Great Vehicle, the supreme wisdom beyond all comparison and equal, and regarding these wisdoms doubting and not believing; yet still believing in sin and merit, and cultivating the roots of goodness, wishing to be born in that land.

There are also beings who accumulate the roots of goodness, seeking the Buddha's wisdom, the universal wisdom, the wisdom beyond all comparison, the inconceivable wisdom of vast majestic virtue, but regarding their own roots of goodness, they cannot give rise to faith.

Therefore, regarding being reborn in the Land of Bliss, their will is hesitant and uncertain, with nothing to rely upon. Yet they still continue mindful without ceasing, binding their roots of goodness as the basis of their vows, and so also attain rebirth.

Because of this condition, though born in that land, they cannot come before the Measureless Lifespan, but stop at the border of the Buddha-land, in the city of seven jewels. The Buddha does not cause them to be so; it is the working of their own bodies and deeds, and the mind's own tendency. There are also jeweled ponds and lotuses, in which they naturally receive their bodies. Food and drink are pleasurable, like the Trayastrimsa heaven.

Yet dwelling within the flower's womb, they cannot come out. For five hundred years they cannot see the Buddha, do not hear the Dharma, and do not see the bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and the holy assembly. Such persons are of unclear wisdom, know few sutras, their minds do not open to understanding, and their minds are not joyful. Therefore, in that land, they are called “womb-born.”

If there are sentient beings who clearly believe in the Buddha's wisdom, and even in the supreme wisdom, cut off doubt and confusion, believe in their own good roots, perform various meritorious deeds, and with utmost sincerity dedicate [the merit], all of them, within the lotus flowers of the pond of seven jewels, sit cross-legged, are miraculously born of themselves, and emerge in an instant. Their bodily marks are radiant, and their wisdom and merit are fully accomplished, like the bodhisattvas.

Maitreya, you should know that those who are miraculously born are so because of their superior wisdom. As for the womb-born, for five hundred years they do not see the Three Jewels, do not know the practice of the bodhisattvas, cannot cultivate merit, and have no occasion to serve Amitābha Buddha. You should know that such persons, in their past lives, lacked wisdom — this is caused by doubt.

blocks.text: Chapter Forty-One: When Delusion Is Exhausted, One Sees the Buddha

inline.s: It is like a wheel-turning sage-king who has a prison of seven jewels; when a prince commits an offense, he is confined within it. With storied towers and ornate
(qǐ, ornate)

halls, jewelled canopies and golden couches, balustrades, windows, and seats, adorned finely and strangely. His food and clothing are like the wheel-turning king's, but with golden chains fettering his two feet. Do the young princes rejoice in this or not?

Maitreya replied: No, World-Honored One. While thus imprisoned, his mind is not at ease; only by various expedients does he wish to seek release. He entreats the ministers near him, but in the end it does not accord with his mind. Only when the wheel-turning king is pleased does he obtain liberation.

The Buddha told Maitreya: These sentient beings are exactly the same. If any have fallen into doubt and regret, and regarding the Buddha's various wisdoms or their own good roots cannot give rise to faith, then — because they did give rise to faith upon hearing the Buddha's name — although they are born in that land, within the lotus flower they cannot appear.

That place of the flower's womb is like a garden, park, or palace in the mind. Why? Within it is pure, without all filth and evil. Yet for five hundred years they do not see the Three Jewels, cannot make offerings and serve the Buddhas, and are far from all supreme good roots. Taking this as suffering, they do not give rise to joy.

If these sentient beings recognize the root of their offense, deeply repent and reproach themselves, and seek to leave that place, then when the faults of their past lives are entirely done away, they come out. Thereupon they can go to the place of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life and hear the sutras and Dharma. After a long time they too will open to understanding and rejoice, and will also be able to make offerings to countless, immeasurable Buddhas and cultivate various meritorious deeds.

Maitreya, you should know that doubt is a great injury to the bodhisattvas and a loss of great benefit. Therefore one should clearly believe in the Buddha's unexcelled wisdom and in one's own good roots.

Maitreya said: How is it that a class of sentient beings in this world, though they too cultivate good, do not seek rebirth [there]? The Buddha told Maitreya: These sentient beings are of shallow wisdom. They discriminate that the Western [land] is not as good as the heavenly realms; therefore, [finding] it not delightful, they do not seek rebirth there. Maitreya said: These sentient beings discriminate falsely. If they do not seek the Buddha-land, how can they escape the wheel of rebirth?

The Buddha said: The good roots they have planted cannot be freed from marks; they do not seek the Buddha's wisdom, and are deeply attached to worldly pleasures and human blessings. Though they cultivate merit seeking the fruits of humans and gods, when they receive the retribution, everything is abundant, yet they cannot escape from the prison of the three realms. Even if parents, wives and children, men and women, and relatives wish to save and redeem them, the king of karma of wrong views they cannot abandon; they remain always in the wheel of rebirth, and are not at ease.

You see that foolish people, who do not plant good roots but only with worldly cleverness and sharp eloquence increase their perverse minds — how can they escape the great calamity of birth and death? There are also sentient beings who, though they plant good roots and create a great field of merit, seize upon marks and discriminate, with emotional attachments that are deep and heavy; seeking to escape the wheel of rebirth, in the end they cannot.

If one plants the roots of all virtues with markless wisdom, with body and mind pure and far from discrimination, seeking rebirth in the pure land and going toward the Buddha's bodhi, one shall be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss and forever attain liberation.

The Bodhisattva Maitreya said to the Buddha: In this Sahā world, and in the various Buddha-lands, how many are the non-retrogressing bodhisattvas who shall be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss? The Buddha told Maitreya: In this world there are seventy-two hundred koṭis of bodhisattvas who have already made offerings to countless Buddhas, planted the roots of all virtues, and shall be born in that land. As for the lesser bodhisattvas who cultivate merit and shall be reborn there, they are beyond reckoning.

Not only the bodhisattvas of my land shall be reborn in that land; in the Buddha-lands of other directions it is likewise so. From the Buddha-land of Universal Light, one hundred and eighty koṭis of great bodhisattvas (bodhisattva-mahāsattvas) are born in that land. In the northeast, from the Buddha-land of the Jewel-Reliquary, there are ninety koṭis of non-retrogressing bodhisattvas who shall be born in that land. From the Buddha-lands of Immeasurable Sound, Radiant Light, Nāga and Deva, Supreme Power, the Lion, Free from Dust, the Crown of Virtue, the Benevolent King, and the Flower Banner — the non-retrogressing bodhisattvas who shall be reborn there are several tens of hundreds of koṭis, or several hundreds of thousands of koṭis, even up to ten thousand koṭis.

The twelfth Buddha, named Unexcelled Flower, has countless assemblies of bodhisattvas, all non-retrogressing. Of sharp and mighty wisdom, they have already made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas, are endowed with great vigor, and have set out toward the one vehicle. Within seven days they are able to grasp the method of steadfastness cultivated by great beings for hundreds of thousands of koṭis of kalpas. Such bodhisattvas shall all be reborn [there].

The thirteenth Buddha, named Fearless, has seven hundred and ninety koṭis of great bodhisattvas, and lesser bodhisattvas and bhikṣus and so forth, beyond reckoning, who shall all be reborn [there]. The names of the Buddhas in the worlds of the ten directions, and the assemblies of bodhisattvas who shall be reborn, if one merely recited their names, the kalpas would be exhausted before [all] were told.

The Buddha told Maitreya: Behold those bodhisattvas-mahāsattvas who well obtain benefit. If there are good men or good women who, hearing the name of Amitābha Buddha, give rise to a single thought of loving joy, take refuge and gaze in reverence, and practice as taught, you should know that such persons gain great benefit and shall obtain the merits described above. Their minds are neither inferior nor arrogant; the good roots they accomplish are all increasing. You should know that such persons are not of the lesser vehicle, and in my Dharma are called the foremost disciples.

Therefore I tell you — gods, humans, and asuras of the world — you should love to practice and give rise to a mind of rare longing. Toward this sutra, give rise to the thought of a guide. Those who wish to cause immeasurable sentient beings to quickly abide and attain non-retrogression, and who wish to behold that vast and adorned, supremely sublime Buddha-land that receives [beings] and perfects their merits, should arouse vigor and listen to this Dharma-gate.

For the sake of seeking the Dharma, do not give rise to minds of retreat, capitulation, or flattery and falsehood. Even should you enter a great fire, you should not doubt or regret. Why? Those immeasurable koṭis of bodhisattvas all seek this subtle Dharma-gate, revere and listen to it, and do not give rise to rejection. There are many bodhisattvas who wish to hear this sutra but cannot obtain it. Therefore you should seek this Dharma.

blocks.text: Chapter Forty-Four: Receiving the Prediction of Bodhi

inline.s: If in a future age, even down to the time when the right Dharma is extinguished, there are sentient beings who plant the roots of all good, having already made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas, then because of the added power of those Tathāgatas they can obtain this vast Dharma-gate, grasp and uphold it, and shall obtain the vast, all-encompassing wisdom (sarvajñāna). Within that Dharma they attain vast, supreme understanding and great joy, and widely explain it to others, always delighting in practice.

All good men and good women who are able, with regard to this Dharma — whether they have sought it, are seeking it now, or shall seek it — all obtain beneficial fruit. You should abide in it without doubt, plant the roots of all good, and constantly cultivate practice, so that there is no doubt or obstruction, and one does not enter into the prison made of all kinds of jewels.

Maitreya, beings of great majestic virtue such as these can give rise to faith in the Buddha-Dharma's vast, extraordinary gate. Because they do not hear this Dharma, there are a koṭi of bodhisattvas who retreat from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

If there are sentient beings who, with regard to this scripture, copy it, make offerings, uphold, and read and recite it; who in a moment explain it to others and persuade them to hear it; who do not give rise to sorrow and affliction, and even day and night contemplate that land and the Buddha's merits — they shall never retrogress from the unexcelled Way.

At such a person's death, even if the great-thousandfold world-system were full of a great fire, he can transcend it and be born in that land. Such a person has already encountered Buddhas of the past and received the prediction of bodhi, and is praised by all Tathāgatas alike. Therefore one should single-mindedly believe and accept, and uphold, recite, explain, and practice [it].

blocks.text: Chapter Forty-Five: This Sutra Alone Is Left Behind

inline.s: Now I speak this sutra for sentient beings, causing them to see Amitābha Buddha and his land and all that is within it. All that should be done may be sought [therein]. Do not, after my extinction, again give rise to doubt.

In a future age, when the scriptures and the Way are completely extinguished, I, with compassion and pity, will specially leave this sutra behind, to remain for a hundred years. Those sentient beings who encounter this sutra shall, according to whatever they wish, all attain deliverance.

For a Tathāgata to appear in the world is hard to meet and hard to see. The scriptures and the Way of the Buddhas are hard to obtain and hard to hear. To meet a good spiritual friend and, hearing the Dharma, be able to practice it — this too is difficult. If one hears this sutra and believes, delights in, and upholds it — of all difficulties, there is none surpassing this difficulty.

If there are sentient beings who, upon hearing the Buddha's name, have a pure and compassionate mind, leap up in joy, feel their hair stand on end, or shed tears, it is all because in past lives they have cultivated the Buddha-way; therefore they are not ordinary people.

If, upon hearing the Buddha's name, one is dubious in mind and, with regard to the Buddha's scriptural words, believes nothing at all, such persons have come from the evil realms; their past calamity is not yet exhausted, and they are not yet to be delivered. Hence their minds are dubious and do not believe, that is all.

blocks.text: Chapter Forty-Six: Diligently Cultivate and Firmly Uphold

inline.s: The Buddha told Maitreya: The unexcelled Dharma of the Tathāgatas, the deep Dharma of the ten powers, fearlessness, unobstructedness, and non-attachment, and the bodhisattva Dharma of the pāramitās and the like, are not easily met. A person able to expound the Dharma is also rare. And [one with] firm, deep faith is likewise hard to encounter.

Now I expound in accordance with principle this vast and subtle Dharma-gate, praised by all the Buddhas. I entrust it to you to make great protection [for it], for the benefit of all sentient beings in the long night. Do not let sentient beings fall into the six realms and bear all manner of peril and suffering.

You should diligently cultivate and practice, following my instruction. Be filial toward the Buddha and constantly mindful of the teacher's kindness. Let this Dharma long abide without being extinguished. Firmly uphold it; do not damage or lose it. Do not falsely add to or subtract from the scriptural Dharma.

If you constantly think without ceasing, you will attain the Way swiftly. My Dharma is thus, and thus I speak. What the Tathāgata practices, you too should follow in practice. Planting and cultivating merit and goodness, seek rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.

blocks.text: Chapter Forty-Seven: Only with Merit and Wisdom Does One First Hear

inline.s: At that time the World-Honored One spoke a verse, saying:
If in past lives you did not cultivate merit and wisdom, you cannot hear this right Dharma now; but having made offerings to the Tathāgatas, you can rejoice and believe in this matter.

The evil, the proud, the indolent, and the wrong-viewed — hard for them to believe the Tathāgata's subtle Dharma. It is like a blind man always dwelling in darkness, who cannot lead another on the road.
Only those who have planted many virtues before the Buddhas can cultivate the deeds that save the world. Hearing it, they uphold it and copy it, recite, praise, and expound it, and make offerings.

Thus, yearning single-mindedly for the pure land, one is certainly reborn in the land of Ultimate Bliss. Even if a great fire filled the three thousand worlds, riding the Buddha's majestic virtue, all can be transcended.
The Tathāgata's deep and vast ocean of wisdom — only Buddhas and Buddhas can know it. Śrāvakas, for koṭis of kalpas pondering the Buddha's wisdom, with all their spiritual powers cannot fathom it.

The Tathāgata's merits the Buddha knows within himself; only the World-Honored One can reveal them. A human body is hard to gain, a Buddha hard to meet; faith and wisdom to hear the Dharma — the hardest of the hard.

If sentient beings are to become Buddhas, their practice must transcend Samantabhadra's to reach the farther shore. Therefore, you learned and wise ones, should believe my teaching as the truth I speak.

Having been so fortunate as to hear this wonderful Dharma, constantly remember the Buddha and give rise to joy. Upholding it, one broadly crosses the stream of birth and death; the Buddha says such a one is a true good friend.

blocks.text: Chapter Forty-Eight: Believing, Accepting, and Practicing

inline.s: At that time, when the World-Honored One had spoken this sutra, in the worlds of gods and humans there were twelve-thousand koṭi-koṭis of sentient beings who, far from the dust and defilement, obtained the pure Dharma-eye. Twenty koṭis of sentient beings obtained the fruit of the anāgāmin. Six thousand eight hundred bhikṣus, with all their outflows exhausted, attained liberation of mind. Forty koṭis of bodhisattvas, abiding in non-retrogression from the unexcelled bodhi, adorned themselves with the merit of the vast vow. Twenty-five koṭis of sentient beings attained the patient endurance of non-retrogression. Four koṭi-koṭis of hundreds of thousands of sentient beings, who had never before given rise to the will to the unexcelled bodhi, now for the first time gave rise to it. Planting good roots and wishing to be born in the land of Ultimate Bliss to see Amitābha Buddha, they shall all be reborn in that Tathāgata's land, and in various directions shall successively become Buddhas, all named Wonderful Sound Tathāgata.

Moreover, in the Buddha-lands of the ten directions, whether they are now being born [there] or shall be born in the future, those who see Amitābha Buddha — in each case there are eighty koṭi-koṭis of persons who receive the prediction, obtain the patient endurance of the Dharma, and accomplish the unexcelled bodhi. Those sentient beings, all by the karmic connection of Amitābha Buddha's past vows, shall all be reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.

At that time the great-thousandfold world-system shook in six ways, and there appeared all kinds of rare spiritual transformations, radiating a great light that illumined the ten directions. Further, the gods, in the sky, made wonderful music and gave forth sounds of rejoicing. Even the gods of the form realm all heard it and praised it as never before. Countless wonderful flowers rained down in profusion.

The venerable Ānanda, the Bodhisattva Maitreya, and the various bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, the eight classes of gods and dragons, and all the great assembly, hearing what the Buddha had spoken, were all greatly delighted, believed, accepted, and practiced [it].
